reason: The edition settled abbreviated allegations and the lemmata that the image-only reading had left uncertain, and showed where the manuscript departs from the print.
sources: Dyni Muxellani Commentarius in regulas iuris pontificii, Lyon, heirs of Jacopo Giunta, 1563, pp. 127-129 (reg. 21) and 169-171 (reg. 31-32), https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_3qa8GbrPNXYC
Dynus, De reg. iu., 1540, Google Books volume BeisKSGGySgC (search snippets only, used to locate the text)

text:
Source-assisted reading of F-reyc (Brugge, Bisschoppelijk Archief, C516, 2). Reread on the images by a research reader with the Lyon 1563 edition of Dinus de Mugello in hand: fol. [1]r col. b lines 4-16, fol. [1]v col. b lines 1-15, fol. [2]v col. a lines 31-42, fol. [2]v col. b lines 39-44 and catchword. All other lines of the bifolium rest on the image-only first reading and are not given here.
Conventions: (x) expansion; [x] lost or supplied; ? uncertain; | line break. Boxes are native pixels.

Canvas 0, fol. [1]r, col. b, lines 4-16, box 1175,259,2250,1000
[Q]uod semel placuit ampli(us) | displice(re) no(n) potest. In s(ente)n(t)ia | poni p(otes)t ex(emplu)m reg(u)le nam ex quo | semel placuit iudici ea(m) sente(n)|tiam [?] no(n) p(otes)t ult(er)ius displicere | ut p(er) h(oc) possit eam mutare sive sit | iniq(ua) sive equa ut ff. de re iud. l. iu|dex et l. paul(us) et l. pl(?) [?] et l. [?] | [?] de [?] l. i. §. fi. et de pe|nis l. divi fr(atr)es. S(ed) (contra) h(oc) opo(n)it(ur) de l. si | p(re)ses C. q(uomod)o et q(ua)n(do) [iudex] cu(m) si(mi)lib(us). S(ed) di|ci solet et debet refer(r)e utru(m) s(ente)n(t)ia | teneat ipso iure

[?] ff. de | (con)d. ob ca(usa)m. Ite(m) p(otest) [?] in elect(i)o(n)e na(m)? | postquam in scrutinio no(m)i(n)avi aliq(ue)m | et electio fuit subsecuta et postq(uam)

Canvas 3, fol. [2]v, col. a, lines 31-42, box 382,1750,1063,2330 (lemma also in box 330,1640,1100,1900)
[C or E]um quis certus est certiora|ri ult(er)ius no(n) oportet. Cavet(ur) | in iur(e) q(uod) venditor qui sciv[it] | servitutem deb(er)i a p(re)dio vendito | c(er)tior(ar)e d(ebet) e(m)ptore(m) al(ias) te(netur) actione [...]|to ad int(er)esse e(m)ptoris. h(oc) v(er)um si e(m)pto[r] | ignoravit servitutem deb(er)i s(ed) si c(er)t(us) | fuit servitute(m) deb(er)i no(n) o(portet) eu(m) c(er)tio|rari ut ff. de act. e(m)p. l. i. §. vendi(tor) | et §. fi. Ite(m) qui ma(n)cipia vendit c(er)ti|orare d(ebet) e(m)ptore(m) de morbis et viciis | al(ias) tene(tur) actio(n)e ve(n)di(ti) vel q(uan)to (minoris) s(ed) | si e(m)ptor intelligat vel i(n)tellige(re)

Canvas 3, fol. [2]v, col. b, lines 39-44 and catchword, box 1086,1900,2000,2750
[N]on l(icet) actori q(uod) reo licitu(m) no(n) ex|istit. Legiste ponu(n)t ex(emplu)m h(uius) r(egul)e | quia si actori pete(n)ti dat(ur) dil(ati)o | p(ro)pt(er) testes (er)go et reo q(uod) ex(emplu)m locu(m) | h(abe)ret si r(egula) poneretur affi(rma)tive v(idelicet) q(uod) | l(icet) actori d(ebet) lice(re) et reo multo pl(us)
Catchword: [ap]parere? p(otest)? in ex   (first word uncertain; two image-only readers gave "p(re)terere ... iii ex" and "Apparere p(otest) iii ex")
